key_insight: A portable, marker-less multi-camera capture system enables accurate 3D reconstruction of hands and manipulated objects in unconstrained, in-the-wild scenes, producing data that better reflects real-world egocentric interactions.
problem_solved: Existing hand–object interaction datasets are mostly studio-captured and lack environmental diversity, limiting model generalization to real-world egocentric scenarios.
method: Design and deploy a portable, marker-less multi-camera rig to collect multi-view egocentric footage with near-unconstrained mobility.
Apply a multi-view 3D reconstruction and hand–object pose estimation pipeline to recover accurate 3D hand and object geometry without markers.
Aggregate reconstructions into a large, diverse in-the-wild dataset and provide benchmarks for hand–object interaction modeling.
impact: Provides practitioners with realistic 3D training data and benchmarks that improve model robustness and generalization for egocentric manipulation tasks, enabling better performance in real-world AR/robotics/interaction applications.

paper_title: SHOW3D: Capturing Scenes of 3D Hands and Objects in the Wild
paper_authors: Patrick Rim, Kevin Harris, Braden Copple, Shangchen Han, Xu Xie
